Only allow alcohol to be sold in pubs and in wine stores between certain times
, I believe alcohol should:

1) only be sold in pubs

2) only be sold in wine stores between certain times, I believe the ease in accessibility to purchase alcohol is ridiculous. I am aware that alcohol may never be banned, but I think there should be restrictions, given how highly addictive it can be.

These rules would mean alcohol wouldn’t be in local corner shops and supermarkets and wouldn’t be being delivered by food delivery services. I have seen alcohol take over people's lives and it can lead to a loss of life. Alcohol can be very addictive and addiction can happen to anyone. By putting these restrictions on this, the NHS could also benefit.

Create an NHS staff recruitment agency, We urge the government to take immediate action in addressing the NHS's costly reliance on external for-profit staff recruitment agencies., Supporting the establishment of an NHS-run recruitment agency & mandating its use for all NHS staff hiring could enable the NHS to save billions of pounds yearly.

In 2019-2020, £6.2 billion was spent on temporary staff, with a significant portion going to agency fees. External agency staff receive higher pay than NHS staff, causing disparity and driving existing staff away, leaving the NHS more dependent on agencies. Savings could be used to increase existing staff wages. We believe that outsourcing recruitment perpetuates a financially unsustainable model that hinders the NHS's ability to deliver cost-effective, high-quality healthcare to the public.

Do not reduce the Right to Buy discount, Stop the reduction of the Right to Buy discount. The Government have said the maximum discount will be reduced to £16,000–£38,000 depending on the tenant's location. We think this is unfair because some people's only way only to get on the housing ladder is via Right to Buy. , We think the Government should look at the ethical side of this, look how it will impact the housing market and look at the long-term effect on people who might have to rent for longer and the impact the economy.

Prevent the reduction of the right to buy discount for long term tenants., Stop the drastic reduction of the maximum right to buy discount for long term tenants. The proposed minimal discounts are highly unfair for the people that have paid rent and been council tenants for 10 years or more. I would like the Labour Party to reconsider for long term council tenants., It is imperative to maintain the integrity of the Right to Buy scheme, without reducing the discounts that have been pivotal in facilitating the purchase of homes for individuals like myself. Therefore, I am calling for support from all to oppose these proposed cuts, ensuring that homeownership remains accessible to all council tenants. I encourage you to sign this petition, join our cause, and stand by us as we strive for homeownership.

Stop local councils from selling social housing to private investors, To ban the sale of social housing by local councils to private investors., Let's get enough signatures and get this debated to protect our remaining council properties.

Establishment of Minimum Standards for Student Housing, We want the government to establish minimum criteria for student houses for landlords to rent them. We think this should include councils investigating all student properties before tenants move in. Properties that do not meet the criteria should not be rented., In our view, it is a national problem that students face everyday. We think it has had detrimental mental and physical health impacts for young people and landlords continue to make extensive profit from the issue.

Review Tax Credit Overpayment system, Tax Credit Overpayments may be claimed many years even decades after the tax credits were paid. The HMRC can take money away from benefit payments. We think this needs to be reviewed by an impartial party., When applying for tax credits, claimants have to send the government relevant information. Every year this is reviewed and updated. Years, even decades later, money can be taken out of benefits, which is being claimed is for alleged overpayments.

We want a review to look at how to give vulnerable claimants a way out of this overpayment system.

Increase statutory maternity pay., I want statutory maternity pay to be raised because of the cost of living. Having a baby doesn't mean bills don't need to be paid. Bills stay the same but often people's income goes down after having a baby. , Some mothers are returning to work too early as they're forced to because they can't afford to pay their bills. Mothers forced to return to work could miss important months with their babies which we believe could be detrimental to their development. Some mothers are also going without meals to be able to afford necessities for the baby.

Provide Funding for Neurodiversity Diagnostic Assessments in State Schools, Provide direct funding for neurodiversity diagnostic assessments in state schools. These could improve diagnosis of students and help them to receive the support they require. This should include funding for the involvement of educational psychologists in the assessment process., Establishing Direct Funding:
Initiate direct funding for neurodiversity diagnostic assessments in primary, secondary, and sixth-form state schools. This should help every student have access to timely and comprehensive evaluations.

Policy Review:
Conduct a thorough review of current policies regarding funding for neurodiversity diagnostic assessments at all educational levels. We believe this will help to address existing gaps and shortcomings.

Restrict the use of disclaimers by police to relinquish ownership of dogs, Currently police can seize dogs under section 1 of the Dangerous Dogs Act (DDA) and can then ask the owners to relinquish ownership by agreeing to sign a disclaimer. We want police not to be allowed to use these disclaimers until a dog has been assessed for type., Many dogs are seized under section 1 of the DDA on the reporting from a member of the public for looks alone. They aren’t banned breeds at this point, they are suspected. An owner may not be present and disclaimers could be signed by another household member or in panic by the owner not aware of their legal rights.

Once a disclaimer has been signed the dog can be euthanised without the opportunity for the owner to appeal. This risks Dogs not of a banned type being destroyed. Disclaimers should not be used at the point of seizing, but only after the dog has been assessed for type.
Abolish the tv licence, We think the BBC (British Broadcasting Corporation) is losing its popularity and we shouldn't be forced to fund it.,

Extend the Freedom of Information Act to Registered Social Landlords (RSLs), We think RSLs exercise functions similar to those of local authorities but are not subject to the same scrutiny. We think this right could enable tenants and residents to obtain risk assessments, safety certificates, and other documents vital to holding RSLs (and their subsidiaries) to account., We think this goal can be achieved by amending the Renters' Rights Bill to designate RSLs (and their subsidiaries) in England and Wales as public authorities for the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act. A similar amendment to the Social Housing Act was proposed in the last parliament.

In Scotland, RSLs are already designated public authorities for the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act.
Increase the DWP Christmas bonus for benefit claimants to £20, Increase the amount given for Christmas bonus. Increase the amount to £20,

Ban in-game currency from video games, We the undersigned would like the government to ban video/mobile games from having in-game/premium currency, and require local currency to be used (the currency where the game is being played)., We think in-game currency in games is an incredibly predatory tactic and could be used to disguise from the purchaser how much they are actually spending. We think there is no inherent benefit of premium currency and that it just confuses and distracts. Alongside this, we think premium currency is often bundled strategically so that the amount you buy is either just not enough for an in-game purchase which means you end up buying a more expensive pack or it will be just too much so you have some left and then feel inclined to buy more.

Ban the use of prong dog collars, I would like the Government to take action on the use of prong dog collars by introducing a ban and issuing fines to those who use them. We also think dogs should be taken away from their owners if they repeatedly offend.
, We do not see the collars as gentle training tools. We think they are abusive to use and are too normalised. They can cause injury to dogs and there are other ways to safely train an animal.

Do not deduct housing element of Universal Credit, I believe that people who are living with parents should get the same as a single person living on their own because they still need the money to pay for their own bills and transportation to and from interviews, job centre appointments and for health appointments., Currently, those living with parents receive lower UC payments as they lose the housing element of the payment. I would like the Government to change this and ensure that those living with parents or other close relatives still receive the full payment. I think this is unfair as these people may still have to pay for transport to attend appointments within the job centre, if they do not drive and rely on public transport. The person also need to keep themselves fed as well.

Ban ground rent on all leasehold properties., I would like the government to introduce a bill which builds on the Leasehold Reform (Ground Rent) Act 2022 and Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024, extending the ground rent ban to all current leaseholds. , A large proportion of flats and apartments are leasehold. This means that if people live in flats or apartments, they can often be faced with ground rents which can be an additional expense, one not faced by those in freehold properties. We believe they should be completely outlawed.

Change the house purchasing process to protect sellers, We believe that buyers should be legally required to cover the seller's legal costs if the buyer pulls out of a property purchase after an offer is accepted., In England and Wales there is no legal requirement for a buyer to cover a seller's costs if the buyer pulls out of a house purchase, even if the process has lasted many months. This can leave sellers with legal costs of hundreds of pounds to find.

Change laws around amendments on birth certificates, I want the Government to change the law so that corrections to a birth registration are made to the relevant part of the full birth certificate, not in a marginal note., If a registrar makes a mistake in entering the sex of a child this cannot corrected on register itself, only in a note in the margin. This may affect the child's future making life difficult for them when getting married, applying for jobs and everything else they need a birth certificate for.

Ban Variable Direct Debits, Ban the use of Variable Direct Debit. We think this leaves consumers in an unfair position as they may get multiple bills and multiple amounts are taken from their bank account per month.,

Allow employees to deduct living expenses from salary before it’s taxed., I’d like to propose that the Government allow employees to deduct essential living expenses—such as rent/mortgage, utility bills, food, council tax and childcare—from their income before it is subject to tax. , I believe this change could bring about several key benefits 1) Increase in disposable income. 2) Reduction in financial stress 3) Fairer taxation system. I believe that the tax system has loopholes for the rich and some large companies do not pay a fair amount of tax. I also think that a large percentage of tax is wasted, and it is therefore only fair to let people keep more of their income, and funding this could include reducing public services.

Devolve The Crown Estate In Wales, We are calling on the Government to devolve the Crown estate from Westminster to Wales, like it was devolved to Scotland in 2017. We believe that the appointment of a Crown Estate Commissioner doesn't go far enough, and that a radical change is needed by devolving the Crown Estate., The crown estate profits from resources in Wales, yet the profits don't go to Wales directly. We feel that this is a clear example of wealth that's being generated in Wales being extracted away over the border.

We believe the money generated in Wales through the Crown Estate can and should be used exclusively to help invest in communities in Wales and help invest in matters like infrastructure, the NHS, Community projects etc.

Require rent increases to be based on inflation and salaries, freeze for 3 years, I call on the Government to place a limit on increases to rent for lettings or landlords, with no possibility to increase rent for the next 3 years. Also, strengthen requirements around landlords communicating with tenants to make them effective., We think it would help reduce homelessness.

Require companies put political party logo on all products if they fund a party, We think people will happily show their desire not to consume or purchase goods that have been made by a company with ties or donations to a political party they do not agree with., We think if companies want to put money towards a party they should be required to show this on all their products and take the hit if consumers boycott their product.

Prohibit publishers irrevocably disabling video games they have already sold, The government should update consumer law to prohibit publishers from disabling video games (and related game assets / features) they have already sold without recourse for customers to retain or repair them. We seek this as a statutory consumer right., Most video games sold can work indefinitely, but some have design elements that render the product non-functional at a time which the publisher controls, with no date provided at sale. We see this as a form of planned obsolescence, as customers can be deprived of their purchase and cannot retain or repair the game. We think this practice is hostile to consumers, entirely preventable, and have concerns existing laws do not address the problem.  Thus, we believe government intervention is needed.

Review the prescribing and sale of topical corticosteroids, We ask the government to review prescribing protocols and over-the-counter availability of topical corticosteroids. We believe that topical corticosteroids have been over-prescribed and irresponsibly prescribed for decades – leading to what is known as ‘Topical Steroid Addiction’., This can cause the iatrogenic illness known as ‘Red Skin Syndrome’ – often misdiagnosed as ‘worsening eczema’. 

The recovery process - ‘Topical Steroid Withdrawal’ is brutal, highly debilitating, and often lasts for years. Healthcare professionals need to fully understand the potential serious side-effects of these medications before prescribing them to patients, to prevent unnecessary, preventable suffering.

Exemption from stamp duty changes if mortgage offers predate the Autumn budget, Waive stamp duty increases for buyers with mortgage offers predating the decision to increase stamp duty in the Autumn budget. We think that if buyers can prove that purchase offers and mortgage offers were agreed before these changes were announced, the higher rates of stamp duty should be waived., Many may now face unexpected costs, which could leave them unable to move. I want to support fairness for those who budgeted under previous rules and are now impacted by government changes. I think this could cause profound disruption to individuals and families who have reserved newbuild homes that won't be built/completed until after the changes come into effect.

Referendum on whether to abolish the Welsh Parliament, I believe a referendum in Wales is needed on whether to abolish the Welsh Parliament., I believe money in Wales is being wasted by the Welsh Government and it has become too costly and is no longer fit for purpose. I think that abolishing it would save money that could be put to better use.

Boost the UK economy & reduce unemployment by reducing corporation tax, I believe that lowering corporation tax to 1% could encourage foreign investment potentially boosting the UK economy and reducing unemployment., I believe we should lower corporation tax to encourage foreign investment.

Extend Right to Buy to Housing Association Residents., The Government should extend the statutory “Right to Buy” to Housing Association tenants in England on the same basis as council tenants., I believe that it will give people who wouldn't normally be able to purchase a property the chance to buy their property. A voluntary pilot ran for a small period of time and then was closed. I think that Housing Association tenants don't have the same rights as council tenants, and are at an unfair disadvantage.

Review of Universal Credit and Job Centre Operations, We urge the UK Government to review Universal Credit and Job Centre operations. We believe there are issues with delays, sanctions, and support which can negatively impact claimants. We want to see improvements in staffing, payment resolutions, and help for disabled and vulnerable people., This petition is deeply personal to those whose lives may have been impacted by mistakes or poor treatment in the system. We believe that a review, followed by reform is essential to help protect vulnerable people, restore dignity to claimants, and ensure staff are better equipped and better supported to do their jobs effectively.

We want to create a system that better serves those in need.

Allow conjugal visits for prisoners in England and Wales, Allow prisoners to have conjugal visits with their partners. We think this will put less strain on relationships and might also help keep prisoners in check as they could lose rights for certain visits if misbehaving., The UK has one of the highest rates of re-offending in the western world. We think it could be beneficial for prisoners to be allowed time to de-stress with their partner. It could also help couples who are looking to start a family, especially if the prisoner has a long sentence.

Abolish inheritance tax for everyone, There is a petition asking for an abolition of inheritance tax for farmers. I call for it to be abolished completely. When someone dies the family experiences the most stressful experience imaginable. The last thing needed is a tax bill or to be forced to sell family assets to pay it., The OBR In 2024-25 forecasts that IHT will raise £7.5 billion representing 0.7 per cent of all receipts and is equivalent to 0.3 per cent of national income. (1)  £7.5 billion is nothing compared to a government income of £1 trillion. There are better ways to fund this and I have set up petitions for this. It is high time it was abolished completely, if anything, for humanitarian reasons.
(1) https://obr.uk/forecasts-in-depth/tax-by-tax-spend-by-spend/inheritance-tax/

Require all products to show origin of production., The Government should introduce legislation to require all products, including those sold online, to show their origin of production., We think consumers have the right to know where a product is produced upon making a decision to purchase.

Increase the statutory paternity leave allowance for fathers of multiple births, We believe the Government should increase paternity leave allowance for fathers of multiple births, such as in the case of twins or triplets. We think it’s unfair that fathers are expected to return to work after two weeks in the event of multiple births., We believe the current policy of 2 weeks for statutory paternity leave is unfair for fathers and mothers and are concerned about the potential mental health impact on mothers. We believe that children from multiple births require a huge amount of care a devotion from both parents, not just one parent. We believe that statutory paternity leave should increase per child born.

Put British companies first: only tender government contracts to UK companies, We think the UK Government should ensure all UK government contracts go to UK companies. We think all governments should put their own people first and this will boost the UK economy in lots of ways., We think all central government contracts should go to UK companies even if it costs more.

Provide tax refund for work commute expenses, We call on the Government to introduce a tax refund for commuting expenses, including costs for fuel, public transport, or vehicle maintenance. We believe this would provide financial relief to workers who commute and ensure fairness for those incurring unavoidable travel expenses., We believe commute costs place a significant burden on workers, particularly for those in areas where public transport is limited or expensive. We believe a tax refund on commute costs would make the system fairer, support economic participation, and reduce the financial strain on hardworking individuals. We also believe it recognises that commuting is a necessity, not a luxury, for many workers.

Don’t consider bonus or overtime payments when calculating universal credit, Change the law so that people who claim universal credits & work, don't get penalised if they receive a bonus in work or if they work a small amount of overtime for a special occasion coming up i.e. a child's birthday, xmas., We believe this affects hundreds of thousands of families in the UK especially single parents who are doing their best to work and juggle parenting. If someone got a £300 bonus in work in most cases their UC would be reduced by 65% of the net payment. We think a change is needed to allow for these bonuses to not effect their usual monthly payments.

Recognise gambling as a trade and form of income for child maintenance, We call on the Government to recognise gambling as a trade and professional gamblers as self-employed. We would like the earnings made by professional gamblers to be used to calculate how much child support should be paid., We believe too many single parents are not getting child support payments from parents who are professional gamblers. We would like professional gamblers to be made to declare earnings and pay child support.

Abolish leasehold ownership, We call for the abolition of leasehold ownership in the UK. England and Wales are some of the few countries who adhere to this system of property ownership. We believe abolishing leasehold ownership would liberate leaseholders from this type of ownership which we view as outdated. , We are concerned that leaseholders are left exposed to service charge hikes, ground rents hikes, refusals by some freeholders to extend their leases etc. Many feel they are trapped in flats they cannot sell because of the conditions that come with leasehold ownership.

Reduce income taxes on earnings under £50,000 and increase personal allowance, Reduce the current basic tax rate of 20%, to 10%, for those earning under £50,000 a year, and increase the personal tax-free allowance to £15,000 a year., We believe many are struggling financially. In our view, prices are too high, food and basic necessities cost too much, bills are increasing, people are having to choose between having a warm house or food. We believe young people can't afford to live independently as they could be due to the current personal allowance. We believe the government needs to start thinking about the public and their needs.

Create an employment right to take your leave whenever you want, The UK has people from different backgrounds, and lots of different countries, and we think employees should be allowed to take their leave allowance whenever they deem fit. We think flights can be really expensive, so we think we should be allowed to take our allocated leave whenever we like., We think this would help people to go back and visit family and friends and also make it affordable for long trips as we think it doesn't make sense to pay flight costs that can be high for a short trip.

Reverse restrictions to landlords’ finance cost relief., We call for the Government to remove the restrictions on the tax relief that buy to let landlords are entitled to claim on their mortgage interest. We believe removing it may entice landlords back to the market, increase availability and make rents more affordable., We believe landlords provide an important service and this unfair tax has caused many to leave the sector, resulting in a shortage of rental properties and increase in rents and homelessness. We believe it has resulted in similar dire circumstances that we think happened in Ireland following a similar policy in 2009, which restricted landlords from claiming tax relief on their mortgage interest.

stop MPs expenses and pay increases pay for second homes and bills for homes, to stop all  expenses being claimed   for second homes    and  too be sectioned for   breach's in  breaking or not meeting policy's  pledged, because  the government is wasting too much  money on   expenses and  misleading claims   on   things like   high speed rail 2  etc  and the disabled and the pensioners  suffer  when  money is low   every time    so

Require train companies to provide an unlimited subscription for train travel, We call on the government to implement a national unlimited monthly subscription card for train travel. We think this would reduce car dependency, alleviate traffic congestion, and make rail travel more affordable for everyone, especially those on lower incomes, in line with climate goals., We think we are facing a climate crisis, and reducing car use is essential to lowering emissions and achieving sustainability goals. We feel train fares are prohibitively expensive for many, preventing people from choosing greener transport options. We think introducing an affordable monthly subscription card could make train travel accessible for all, reduce congestion, and help the UK become a global leader in climate action and help set an example to the rest of the world’s nations.

Require train operators to allow under 18s to purchase child tickets, We think this should happen because for other things, e.g. buying cigarettes, voting, people have to be 18. Why should young people be considered adults at 16 for a train journey?, We think it is not fair that 16 and 17 year olds are considered adults when it comes to money for train fares. We think it should be 18 like it is for other things!

UK Government To Create A British International Rail Company., With international trains no longer serving Kent International Stations such as Ebbsfleet & Ashford International & talks about new services & operators coming to HS1 via Europe destinations, we think the UK Government should create & run their own Great British Railways International., Currently there is no competition on HS1, and we think there is a demand for International services through mainly Ashford International & in future Ebbsfleet International for people & residents of the Southeast of England, as well Tourists coming to the UK via Kent. We think with competition, maybe the UK could have its own International service from London St Pancras via HS1 to destinations in Europe via both Kent stations, at a reasonable price.

Impose a lifetime ban on animal ownership for anyone convicted of animal cruelty, The government should impose a lifetime ban on animal ownership for anyone who causes deliberate suffering to animals. Under current laws, courts can impose bans but these may be short-term, allowing offenders to own animals again after a short period., We think anyone who harms an animal should never be trusted with one again.
 
We think there is no reason to believe that a person who has shown a capacity for cruelty will change, especially without proper rehabilitation. We believe a lifetime ban could ensure that once an individual is convicted of animal abuse, they will never again have the power to inflict harm on another animal under their ownership. Animal ownership is a privilege, not a right, and cruelty shouldn't be tolerated.

Provide funding to help the television industry and support TV freelancers, The British TV industry has faced a decline in recent years, leaving some freelancers jobless for long periods, unable to support their families, and exiting the industry., The government could offer financial aid to freelancers during gaps, provide tax incentives for broadcasters to resume commissioning earlier, and invest in creative industries to create new opportunities. We think that legislation should prevent public sector broadcasters from halting commissions in ways that harm the workforce. 
 
Reforms ensuring fair contracts and protections for freelancers, alongside support for training and upskilling, could also help retain talent and revive the struggling TV industry.

Save Smithfield and Billingsgate markets., Reinstate the long term future of the current markets or at least provide an alternative site. Hundreds of businesses and thousands of jobs depend on these markets., The Corporation of London has voted to close Smithfield and Billingsgate markets while abandoning plans of a relocation site. This will leave thousands potentially unemployed and close many businesses. Not just those of the market traders but also for the small businesses that operate using the markets. Both markets are vital to food supply for London and large surrounding areas, have been operating for hundreds of years and support thousands of jobs which are now in jeopardy.

We Want Affordable Housing for All., We request for the government to statutorily provide a decent, high standard of affordable housing for everyone. Presently, some people cannot afford housing, as they need to save up deposits and we think the rents are too high., We think it is about time that affordable housing was recognised as a basic human right! We think the government need to act on this by building or renovating housing, so it is accessible for all, from families to young people leaving home. We think everyone should be able to afford to rent a decent home.
 
We believe that the Right to Buy Scheme, on the surface appeared to be a positive idea, however the money from the sale of council housing was never used to invest in enough new housing, thus potentially leading to increased homelessness.

Make the purchase and resale of practical driving tests illegal., Make it illegal to buy and resell driving test dates due to the impact it’s having on the ability to book a driving test., People describing themselves a “driving test brokers” are buying and reselling tests making it incredibly difficult to book a driving test using bots to book tests before any person can. I need one for my job and can not book a test. These self claimed “brokers” are selling test dates at prices up to £400 and a lot of these test sales are scams. It is breaking the country, making it difficult for those who need it and in plain words is the work of greed and laziness.

Means test the MPs for expenses, Stop the MPs in parliament receiving expenses, They are earning 93000 per year we pay the rent on their second home they should pay their own heating water and food bills

Members of Parliament should not claim any expenses except rent on a second home, I would like the government to enact the necessary changes to ensure members only claim rent on their second home, I feel the country is in a dire financial situation and they should set a goood example

Allow England to have a devolved parliament, Allow England to govern itself the same as Scotland,Wales and Northern Ireland, I feel the people of England don't really get a say in how they want they're country to be run

Pause Employment Rights Bill to assess impacts on SMEs, The Regulatory Policy Committee assessed eight of the twenty-three individual Impact Assessments for the Bill as “not fit for purpose”, six of which fall within the ‘highest impact’ measure category in the Bill’s summary impact assessment., Small businesses are already facing increased costs from higher minimum wages, increased National Insurance, rents, rates, utility bills etc. We are concerned that the implementation of this bill could be the tipping point. We demand that the government slow down, reevaluate, and consult with SME owners. We believe it is crucial to rethink this to prevent irreversible damage to our small businesses.

Require rail customers to be told the cheapest possible fare, We think the UK Government should require train companies to give customers information on the cheapest possible fare as a matter of course and recognize the vital role of the existing ticket office estate in delivering on this aim., We think the current system of pricing for rail fares is complex. As such we think it is difficult for the customer, especially in a digital purchase environment, to be assured that they are getting the best fares. I would like the UK government to recognise the vital role of ticket offices and inclusive opening hours to improve the delivery of face to face advice to passengers to reduce the rail fare system complexity and ensure best value.

Reduce council tax by 50% for single persons, I think that the single persons council tax discount should be set at 50% reduction instead of 25%., I feel this should be done due to the cost of living, increases in tax and the pressure of single people and single parents face.
 
I believe we have the same bills as everyone else but with only 1 wage coming in.
 
I think the single person discount should be set at 50% which would be fair considering you are single and not in a couple.

ALL MP’s should not be allowed to claim ANY expenses on their properties, With the government stopping the WFA for our elderly, all MP’s  should not be allowed to claim expenses for rent/ utility bills / mortgages on their properties., This isTax payers money they are using and it should not be allowed.

Government to set out plans for reducing rail fares, The government recently announced a rise of up to 4.6% in rail fares, explaining that people are willing to pay for a good service. We believe that fares for commuters are far too high and not sustainable for working people., We want the government to set out plans for reducing fares overall, and for the introduction of more fare options, which they can implement once most passenger train operators are brought into public ownership. We think these plans should focus on peak fares during commuting times. We believe this could help boost productivity in the UK, since many businesses require workers to travel into the office and high rail fares can be a barrier for this to happen.

We want the Government to grant birth parents the right to have adoptions review, We want the Government to respect the rights of the child and create a right for birth parents to ask for a case to be revisited where their circumstances have changed. We believe it is important to recognise that people change.,

Ban booking fees for all entertainment venues and events , Pass a law to prohibit booking fees. We think the price advertised must be the total price you pay., We believe it is misleading to consumers to purchase something then get told just prior to payment there is an additional charge to just buy the ticket.

Introduce conveyancing laws similar to those in Scotland, across England & Wales, I urge the UK Government to introduce laws for the conveyancing process currently used in Scotland to be used across England and Wales. I believe this could speed up property sales and stimulate the economy while reducing the burden on conveyancers and the margin for errors. , I think this could also reduce stress, financial losses, and uncertainty. 
 
I want the Government to adopt Scotland's house buying and selling process in England and Wales as the current system can be archaic, slow, stressful, and often results in wasted time and financial losses due to the burden on conveyancers. 
 
Adapting the process could reduce uncertainty and make transactions quicker and more efficient. I think this change would minimize the risk of mishandling a large volume of cases, ensuring smoother property sales and boosting the economy through faster market turnover.

Public inquiry into the selling of Family Asset Protection Trusts., We think some people are being mis-sold "Family Asset Protection Trusts". We think the Government needs to protect citizens, introduce harsher punishments for miss-selling, and support victims. , We think the Government is not doing enough at the moment, and that this could be the Next Big Miss-Selling Scandal.
 
We think vulnerable people - such as the elderly and the sick - may be being sold these without their effects being properly explained, and that they can leave people worse off.  We believe they are being promised protection from costs - such as care fees - but that what they are being sold may not actually protect them from these costs. We want to see the government hold a public inquiry on this.

Make it a legal requirement for all landlords to hold valid buildings insurance, Under current regulations, landlords who own properties outright are not obliged to hold buildings insurance. Require that all landlords who rent out properties, regardless of mortgage status, maintain valid buildings insurance as a legal condition of letting the property., We believe mandatory buildings insurance would ensure that necessary repairs are funded without placing tenants’ safety and financial security at risk. We think it would also protect local authorities and emergency services from shouldering undue burdens if uninsured damages lead to unsafe conditions. In our view, implementing this measure would improve tenant protection, property standards, and overall fairness in the rental market.

Change Delay compensation times on UK trains from 15 minutes to 10 minutes., The Government should change the minimum time for delay repay to 10 minutes in train franchise contracts. We think this will force a change of operation from operators as it would eat into their share price.
, We believe that we are exposed every day to a bad, overpriced, train service, and yet we have no say or option but to use these monopolies.

We consider that if you are clearly big on "green" then this needs to be sorted out as we think that this type of service just drives people insane and forces them to use a car rather than a train.

Require online retailers to name intended delivery company prior to transaction, We think that consumers should be able to make a decision to purchase goods online based on the delivery company that will be used, before the purchase is completed. We think that the number of parcels stolen/disappearing before delivery is increasing annually., We think it’s wrong that consumers sometimes have to use delivery companies they don't trust. We think it’s the fairest way forward if people are able to decide who to buy from based on the courier company being proposed prior to purchasing the product.

Introduce a law preventing copyrighted work being used to train AI, We believe that creatives need to have ownership over their work. We think there should be a legal opt out scheme that could allow creatives to protect their work,

Ensure football fans hold majority stake in clubs, We want to make the 50+1 rule mandatory within the pro and semi pro leagues in England, which means at least 50% plus one share of a club must be owned by members' associations. ,  We believe this gives fans more control of the club and allows them to have more of a say than an outside investor(s)/ investment group.

We believe this will ensure that English football is fairer and has a better, more stable and sustainable structure of ownership for the future. We feel this will stop investors/ investment groups seeking profit over the needs of the club. 
 
We think this form of ownership has been successful across European countries, such as Germany; which we think is a positive sign that it does work, and it works well.

Provide funding to separate Gynaecology/women’s health from Maternity services, Invest more money into Gynaecology services to make them separate from Maternity and stop 1000s of women who are struggling with infertility or miscarriage going through the heart ache of having to share clinic spaces or wards with pregnant women or parents to be., I recently had a full hysterectomy for stage 4 Endometriosis and although the choice i made was the right choice, after years of trying, i remain childless . My experience was made extremely traumatic by the fact that the ward i was staying on was a mixed women's surgical ward/antenatal ward. I think this is an issue in clinics as well. We often have to share the waiting room with mums and dads to be. I think there needs to be change and funding for separation of Gynaecology clinics from Maternity services.

Cap on interest rises for Mortgages so people don't lose their homes, We think the Government should clamp down on mortgage rate rises for existing mortgages, so when it comes to renewing a mortgage rate there should be a max limit where a bank can raise interest rates on current home owners., We think the Government should bring in a law to do this. This could help prevent people struggling and losing their homes.

Review the affordability of the rental market, We think the affordability of the rental market needs to be reviewed by government. We think the review should consider requiring landlords to offer a discounted rate on rent for single occupants such as 25%, like how council tax is done for single occupants as we think this would be beneficial., As someone who works full time and has no one to share a flat with, I feel renting a 1 bed flat is my only option.

Require RA committee members to reveal conflicts of interest with the Landlord., Amend the 1985 Landlord and Tenant Act to require that individuals holding senior positions within a Residents Association—such as Chairman, Treasurer, or Secretary—must disclose any potential conflicts of interest related to the Landlord or managing agent responsible for collecting Service Charges., I believe there could be instances of corruption within Resident Associations, where committee members could be colluding with managing agents and landlords to misrepresent other association members. By making conflicts of interest transparent, I believe we could reduce the occurrence of dishonest and fraudulent behaviour.

Change the ‘whole month’ approach to change of circumstances in Universal Credit, If a change in circumstance occurs at any point in the Universal Credit assessment period it counts for the whole month - which we think is unfair., It can mean people receive less than they had expected and budgeted for. We think any changes in entitlement should be pro-rata.
 
For example if a child stops being a child 3 days before assessment period ends, the claimant is told they owe money for the whole month due to this change - not just the 3 days the child had stopped being a child. 
We feel the Government may push people in debt with this policy.
We think it would be better if the Government calculated entitlement to the day.

Review the affordability of care homes, We want the government to investigate the affordability of care homes., I do not see how some care homes can justify charges of £5000 to £7000 per month. I think that most of the people in these homes who have to self fund have worked really hard to buy their own homes, only to have to sell them to pay for care costs. Their money can be gone in a matter of years. I feel that this is unfair to them.

Sell Chequers, the country home of the Prime Minister, I propose that the Prime Minister’s country home, Chequers, be sold to raise vital revenue for the country., We believe this country is in desperate financial trouble. The NHS is on its knees, people can’t afford to heat their homes or feed their families and the train network is crumbling. Meanwhile the PM retains his country home, 40 miles from Downing Street. The value of this house and the cost of running it must run into many millions of pounds. Other venues, perhaps Buckingham Palace, could be used for functions that Chequers is used for.

Create a regulatory body for funeral directors , Many families trust funeral directors with the care of their loved owns without knowing they are largely unregulated. My aim is for the government to start the process of creating a regulatory body to ensure our deceased are treated with dignity and respect., There are currently two associations attempting to govern funerals, membership is voluntary and they have no real sanctions available. It can be described as marking your own homework. This is simply not enough. The CMA has looked at the funerals sector, highlighting serious concerns. I believe in some cases our loved ones are being neglected, losing someone is something that will affect all of us at some point in life and I cannot be at peace knowing it continues. Many funeral directors see no issue with regulation. We need this addressed in parliament. We need help from our government.

Environment Agency re dredge the waterways of UK to ease flooding pressures, Get the environment agency to go back to dredging the Thames and other water ways that flood to stop the devastation caused, The government need to do this as I live in Wraysbury in 2014 David Cameron visited and advised ‘we would never allow this to happen again’ fast forward to 2024 and the village is again devastated by flooding, river beds are higher than ever impacting on the problem, the environment agency need to start being proactive rather than reactive, from 1947 till 2003 Wraysbury did not flood. Yes we had rain, storms etc, but the rivers were always dredged, every year, somewhere along the Thames, when they stopped then the river bed levels rose and flooding started.

Give Knighthood to Alan Bates, What a delicious irony it would be to give Alan Bates the now spare CBE - instead of putting it back into the cupboard. Or perhaps a Kighthood!, Alan Bates has worked doggedly for free on behalf of hundreds of innocent victims - against the juggernaught that is The Post Office. A real David & Goliath story if ever there was.

If the CBE gets lost in the post going back, then perhaps consider giving Mr Alan Bates a much deserved knighthood.

He is one person who has earned it.

Review the use of forceps for the delivery of babies, Having suffered a birth injury when my son was born, I believe forceps should not be used in the delivery of babies. Instead I believe women should be offered a caesarean section. , The use of forceps can lead to severe birth tears that damage a woman’s anal sphincter.
 
The use of forceps can lead to life-long complications such as bowel/urinary incontinence and prolapses. 
 
This could possibly mean women are at risk of losing their job and financial independence.
 
Severe tears can lead mothers to develop depression and other mental health issues.
We want the Government to review the use of forceps in the delivery babies, and look at whether their use is still appropriate, and also what information is given to mothers ahead of their use.
All mothers deserve to be able to make an educated choice in the delivery method for their child and not be left suffering the consequences of an uninformed decision.

Force Insurance Companies to do fairer and more affordable car insurance for all, I personally think and many others think car insurance prices are ridiculous, especially young drivers, it’s outright theft that some people can’t get insured on little tiny engined cars for less then £1.000, I want the government to stick up for motorists and force the insurance companies to lower their prices or explore other ways to do so, for instance in other European Countries it’s much more affordable such as Norway, Poland, Germany, Sweden France ext

Do not allow rail fares to be increased, We all want rail fares to remain at current prices as increased fares will hit the people’s pockets, especially during the cost of living crisis, and will also impact many tourists from travelling by train nationwide. If prices rise in March 2024 we think it will be a nightmare for millions., We want the Government to hear our voices and respect our rights to public transport.

Increase threshold for car tax surcharge to cars with a list price of £45,000, We ask the government to raise the threshold for the additional £390 tax from cars with a list price of £40000 to those with a list price of £45000. Many households needing to buy new family sized cars will already be stretching to pay the cost, let alone an extra £32.50 a month., As it stands if you purchase a new car with a retail price of £40,000 or more you will be subject to £390 a year EXTRA road tax bringing it to over £500 a year for some people.
 
Considering inflation being the way that it is, many family size cars are now into and over the £40000 bracket for even some of the more basic models. Especially if you want to purchase a hybrid vehicle to “help the planet” you are likely to be going over the £40000 margin meaning an extra £32.50 per month.

Give the Right to Buy to tenants living in Housing Associations, We want the Right to Buy scheme to be extended to tenants living in Housing Association homes as-well, not just for council homes. We want to be given our right to own our home that we pay rent upon rent for!, The Right To Buy provides tenants with something to show for years of paying rent. When it comes to owning your home, it can if necessary be sold to pay for care later in life, it also gives us less dependency on the state. A home that has been bought can be handed down to your children. If the right to buy was introduced to housing association tenants, it could provide hundreds of thousands of poorer households with the financial security that goes with owning your own home. We deserve our HOME

Prohibit sale of pre workout drinks/supplements containing caffeine to under 16s, Put a law in place the prohibits minors being able to purchase pre-workout drinks and supplements which contain caffeine. , Some pre-workout drinks and supplements contain high levels of caffeine, which can be dangerous, especially to young people, who might not be aware of the potential impact of over consumption. I think that legislation should be introduced to ensure that retailers cannot sell these products to under 16s.

Provide more funding to support postgraduate physician associate students , We believe there should be more funding to support physician associate postgraduate students., The training can be intense with very limited opportunity to take on paid work outside of the course. 
 
The current funding arrangements mean that students may have no money for living costs, including expensive travel costs and other bills.

Require all taxi drivers to take the CPC course, Taxi drivers spend more hours on the road than most other drivers. I believe they should be made to do the CPC to understand the roads and protect passengers better., If bus drivers and lorry drivers have to do the CPC course, then I believe all taxi drivers should have to as well.

They carry passengers and spend as many if not more hours on the road.

Extra care should be taken when carrying passengers.

I believe councils hand out taxi licences too easily, and we should make taxi drivers more qualified to do the job.

Review plan for care costs so people don’t have to sell their homes, The Government is introducing reforms regarding care costs. These should be reviewed to ensure people do not have to sell their homes to cover care costs., I am a homeowner and, like many others in my situation, I face the fear of having to sell my home to cover care costs. 
 
Families who have worked all their lives to afford to buy their own property have  scrimped and saved, usually with view to keeping a roof over their heads, hopefully leaving some inheritance.

Provide financial support for full-time workers with high-interest mortgages, I would like the Government to provide more financial support for full-time workers with high-interest mortgages, many of whom are struggling with debts. Some people's mortgage payments have doubled since 2023, and we feel our standard of living has gone from comfortable to impossible., I work in the construction industry and since mortgage rates have gone up, I feel the industry has suffered. Some people are losing jobs and businesses because many people have stopped building or selling houses. Many cannot afford to buy a house with the current mortgage rates. Some people who work full time are struggling as much as those who get benefits, and I think the Government should provide more support to full-time workers.

Government not to change rules on councils selling community assets, There have been news reports that there may be rules changes regarding the ability of councils to sell off community assets. We believe this must not happen. We think this would be short-sighted and detrimental to the public and local government., We believe that after decades of neoliberalism and privatisation it’s clear to see that selling off assets for short-term cash hurts communities in the long-term. We believe we need to protect our public services and make sure they’re safeguarded for future generations to enjoy as we have.

Require landlords to offer a single person discount on rent , Single occupants are expected to pay the same rates as couples / 2+ income households. Consequently, many single occupants spend a higher proportion of their income on outgoings for rent, effectively being penalised for not cohabiting., I think the Government should legislate so that landlords must provide discounts for single occupant tenants. I think many working individuals, who live on their own, are completely overlooked in society. Single occupants are expected to pay the same rates for rent as 2+ more occupants. This can mean single occupants have less opportunities to save money and end up working more hours to generate income in order to cover the rising rates of cost of living. This is inequality.

Provide funding for train companies to give train drivers a pay rise , The Government should provide funding for train drivers to get a pay rise. They haven't had a pay rise since 2019., Throughout the pandemic, train drivers worked hard and that should be considered by people of UK.

We believe train drivers are hard working individuals who deserve increased pay, and this goal can’t be reached unless they get the support of the people along with the government. Some train drivers have struggled during and after the coronavirus, and some struggle to pay for expenses leaving them with the bare minimum.

Reconnect Louth to the National rail network!, I want the Government to re-open the railway line to Louth, reconnecting the town to the national rail network via the Boston - Skegness (Poacher Line).

This line was rejected for further funding from the Restoring Your Railway Fund from the Department for Transport., I want the Government or Parliament to do it because since Louth has lost it’s rail link completely the town is cut off from the rest of the UK. Today, the nearest railway stations to Louth are either at Grimsby Town or in Market Rasen. There is over 15 miles between Louth and these two stations. I think that a town of this size should have it’s own railway connection with a new station to be built elsewhere in the town as the original station cannot be reused due to several different factors.

Modify Corporation Tax to incentivise smaller wage gaps between staff, This petition asks the Government to change Corporation Tax to a sliding scale, proportional to the relationship between the highest and lowest paid person in a company. The greater the disparity between highest and lowest paid, the greater the tax rate, the smaller the gap, the lower the tax rate., The current Corporation Tax system does not take into account the significant pay differences within companies. Research shows that some CEOs of FTSE 100 companies earn more than 200 times the earnings of their employees, which we believe is detrimental to our society and economy. By implementing this proposed tax system, we can encourage corporations to reduce wage gaps and contribute more equitably to our economy. We believe this will make our tax system fairer and promote good internal company dynamics.

Fund free rail travel for all track operatives, including agency staff, I would like the Government to provide funding for all rail track operatives, including agency staff, to have free rail travel., I want to not have to beg money from friends and family in order to get to work when I am travelling on the very same rails that often i am employed to maintain.

Make short selling shares illegal in the UK, I believe short selling of stocks in the UK causes instability in companies share prices., How on earth can some other company loan out something you own without your consent? I believe that it amounts to legal theft authorised by the government, I think it is open to abuse, and needs to be banned and stopped.

Require train stations to install protection from people falling on tracks, People are being hit by trains far too often. To improve the safety of passengers we believe all stations must have physical protection from people falling onto the train/tube tracks., Please oblige stations to have protection from people falling onto tracks, to save lives.

Stop the renaming of the London Overground, We would like to stop the London Overground from being renamed to the six different names: Lioness, Mildmay, Windrush, Weaver, Suffragette and Liberty., The money being spent for this could be much better used to tackle knife crime, set up a fund for struggling families with their energy bills or many other uses that would be of a direct benefit to Londoners.

The TFL website states that “some” people found the network confusing. This is not a compelling enough argument to use public funds in this way.

Fund construction of new affordable social housing, We urge the Government to provide funding for more affordable social housing, to reduce expenditure on benefits for private housing costs. This initiative aims to assist the less fortunate, disabled and those struggling with addiction, and to foster a more sustainable future for all., We believe addressing the housing crisis is paramount to prevent a deepening cycle of homelessness and social inequality. With private housing costs increasing, we are concerned that failure to act risks not only the well-being of the less fortunate, disabled, and those battling addiction but also financial instability. We think swift investment in affordable social housing is crucial to break this cycle, secure vulnerable populations, and prevent a looming economic downturn.

Do not make rules on owning a crossbow tougher, The Government are considering toughening rules around crossbow ownership. I think people should be at liberty to own a crossbow and that further regulation shouldn't be imposed. Archery can be a cheaper alternative to clay pigeon shooting. Archery is part of our heritage., I think current laws are adequate for the control of crossbows, there were fewer than 10 homicides by crossbow between 2011 and 2021. I think proposed laws are draconian and unjust. There are people in control of firearms, which can be more dangerous. Handguns were banned in the 1997, yet still gun crime still continues. We believe more clubs and education is the key, not tougher rules on owning a crossbow.

Increase statutory maternity leave and pay to 2 years at 75% pay, Amend the law to increase statutory maternity leave and pay for women giving birth to 2 years at 75% pay., I don't believe the current law supports women who give birth enough. I don't believe current entitlement gives them enough time to prepare for returning to work. In some cases, mothers may not be able to find any suitable or sustainable childcare, meaning a return to work could put their child at risk. I think new mums need more time with their newborn to raise and prepare them for life.

Change Statutory Maternity Pay to a percentage of weekly earnings with no cap, I would like Government to increase statutory maternity pay. I think people should receive a percentage of their weekly earnings for a period of 6 months, with no cap. After that period, I think people should receive the standard statutory maternity pay., I think that to expect anyone to be able to live off £172 a week is ludicrous. Households that have two full-time wages coming in are also unlikely to be able to access extra help. If you are a single parent you may be entitled to benefits and can end up better off financially. I think the cap on maternity pay after six weeks should be reconsidered.

Ease restrictions on sale, purchase and possession of Waxed Hexamine Tablets, We want the Government to reform restrictions on hexamine to allow for Waxed Hexamine Tablets to be sold in boxes with a maximum quantity of 3 boxes, without the need for any licence., These tablets are used by some steam toys, and we are concerned about the impact these new restrictions will have on the businesses that manufacture this toys.

Remove VAT on Defibrillators, and related accessories and consumables, To remove the VAT charged on these devices, as they can save the NHS significant amounts as first aid lifesavers, often paid for by charitable donations. We believe they should not be subject to a 20% tax., Many small organisations, sports facilities and clubs provide defibrillators for public use at their own cost. These items are expensive to purchase and require accessories to house them safely, and consumables (pads etc) to keep them safely operational.

Extend Sure Start Maternity Grant and Healthy Start to all working mothers, I am a new mum to a 4-month old I have gone from full-time wage to maternity pay. We believe it is wrong that many working mums don't qualify for these because they don't get benefits or their household income is too high., We believe eligibility for this support shouldn't be about income. I was turned down for Sure Start Maternity Grant which is for people expecting their first child, but because I'm not on benefits I can't get it. If I lived on my own I wouldn't be able to pay bills and feed me and my son. And because my partner earns we can't get help but all his money goes on bills so we struggle for food. It's about time the Government provided more help to working families and working mums who struggle to get by.

Increase compensation available to jurors to cover lost earnings and other costs, We want the Government to increase the amount that can be claimed by jurors to cover lost earnings and the cost of any care or childcare outside of their usual arrangements., Despite all the current increases in living costs, the Government has not increased compensation available for loss of earnings and additional care costs when the public is summoned for jury service. Many people struggle from financial hardship resulting from jury service, and we believe the payments available are far too low.
 
Example. If I was doing jury service for 8 weeks the money received for loss of earnings would not cover my mortgage payments, electricity bills and utility bills.

Change Universal Credit Housing Element Rules when rent is set per week, When someone's rent is set per week, including most social housing tenants, the housing element for Universal Credit is calculated by multiplying this by 52, then dividing by 12. However, some Housing Years there are 53 Mondays in the Year, so when this happens people can go into rent arrears., My rent is going up to be £236.77 per week. If paying monthly, the Housing Association have said its £1045.73 I need to pay. However, Universal Credit (who are paying direct) will only pay £1026, so only paying for 364 days of the year, when there is at least 365, and in a leap year 366.
 
We want the way the housing element for Universal Credit is calculated to be changed, so that this covers the full rent for the year, not missing a day or two.

Require all landlords/agencies to accept tenants claiming benefits, I think that tenants claiming housing benefit / other benefits face discrimination from landlords and letting agents who do not want to rent to them. , I have seen many people who can't find a place to rent because of this. All landlords and agencies should be required to accept tenants claiming benefits and not be allowed to exclude them.
legalise cannabis, make it legal to possess and sell cannabis, prohibition is not working

Allow students to be taken out of school for two weeks a year without penalty, Families face school fines for taking their children out of school to go on affordable holidays. This can be a particular issue for low-income families, and families with children that have additional needs, who want or need to avoid busier and more expensive periods., I feel these families are being discriminated against as they may not find it possible to travel outside of term time, as it could be too costly or overwhelming, with travel, queues, noise, busy airports, busy public transport, busy resorts etc.
 
We think it's unfair that these families and children might not be able to go on holiday because they can't take time off during term time. Parents may also have additional needs that would make travelling at busy times difficult.

Allow jobless overseas healthcare workers in UK to stay for one year, Several health care workers who arrived in UK are left without jobs as their sponsors are unable to provide them with one or that there wasn't a job available for them when they arrived. Some firms lose their licence to sponsor due to their own mistakes., People in the UK who lost their sponsorship are only permitted to stay 60 days. 60 days is a very short notice for a family to arrange departure as it could unsettle their children's schooling, lead to loss of rent or deposit, furnishing costs, air ticket and relocation costs. The request is to extend jobless health workers' stay in the UK for one more year for them to secure another job.

Exclude pre-marriage assets from divorce settlements in England and Wales, In Scotland only assets acquired from the date of marriage up to the date of separation are considered in divorce settlements. This is not the case in England and Wales, where a spouse can be granted rights to assets - such as pensions - acquired before marriage. We want this to change., We believe it is unfair that people who are divorced in England and Wales, with financial assets acquired before their marriage, can be disadvantaged compared to people in Scotland when it comes to divorce settlements. We want pre-marriage assets to be excluded from divorce settlements in England and Wales, to mirror rules in Scotland.

Require a licence to own, breed or sell any dog, We believe a licence should be required for any ownership, breeding or selling of any dog., A licence is currently only required for either of the following:
 
- Breeding 3+ litters of puppies in 12 months and selling any of the dogs
- Running a business that breeds and advertises dogs for sale
 
The idea of requiring a license for any ownership, breeding, or selling of dogs aims to ensure responsible and ethical practices in dog ownership and breeding. While the current regulations focus on specific activities around breeding and selling dogs, we want the Government to bring in legislation to expand the licensing requirement to cover all dog ownership, breeding, and selling, so this is more highly regulated.

Enact legislation to make 'psychologist' a protected title, Anyone can use the title of 'psychologist'. We believe this undermines public trust and contributes to harm. Nine types of 'psychologist' role are protected (i.e. clinical, health), regulated by HCPC and adhere to strict standards. We want any use of the title 'psychologist' to be protected., This situation allows unregulated practitioners to offer 'psychological' services, which we believe poses a risk to the public. There have been reports of unregulated 'psychologists' providing inaccurate ADHD assessments. A senior family court judge, has highlighted the confusion caused by the unregulated use of the title 'psychologist' in family court proceedings. The media also features unqualified 'psychologists' , which we believe risks widespread public harm.

Refund Self Assessment Tax within 10 days for sole traders earning under £100k, We want the Government to provide self-assessment tax refunds within 10 working days of submission for sole traders with less than £100k of turnover. We believe 'security checking' businesses with less than £100k turnover is causing unnecessary delays. , We want the Government to stop wasting time and stop holding on to our money while checking small businesses to make sure they have given a big enough cut of their hard earned money. The Government is withholding our money, until we prove we earned what we earned and we are given no compensation for this. The Government fines us for late submissions and charges penalties up to £1,300 a year for this, it should provide refunds owed within 10 working days.

Reduce the Lifetime ISA withdrawal penalty from 25% to 20%, We want the Government to reduce the withdrawal penalty from a Lifetime ISA from 25% to 20% so savers needing to withdraw for reasons other than first time buying or retirement, are not punished for wanting to reallocate their savings., I believe reducing the withdrawal penalty to 20% would encourage more people to use these saving devices as their savings would not be as constricted. Why should savers be punished by taking a hit on their initial input, for having or needing to withdraw funds for other mitigating reasons? We believe you should be able to get back at LEAST the initial investment if made in a cash LISA.

Require videogame publishers to keep games they have sold in a working state, Require publishers to leave videogames (and related game assets / features) they have sold to customers in a reasonably working state when support ends, so that no further intervention whatsoever is necessary for the game to function, as a statutory consumer right., Many videogames rely on servers. When these are shut down, games can be left unplayable where no action is taken to remove this dependency. We believe this is effectively robbing customers, leaving them with no recourse to retain their purchases. We have concerns that existing laws and agencies do not effectively solve this problem. Thus we believe government intervention is needed to stop this practice.

Raise statutory maternity pay to £250 a week & raise UC during maternity leave, Raise Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) to £250 per week. Increase Universal Credit during maternity, and do not take household income into account (treat all mothers as a single income)., We don’t think that using partners income to assess UC during maternity is fair as income may still affected in that household during maternity. Raise SMP because at the moment it might not even cover bills. Especially with cost of living at the moment. UC to be increased even if they have a partner as income in that household may be affected.

Allow tenants to end tenancy agreement if landlord fails to complete repairs, Enable private tenants to end their tenancy agreement without landlord's permission if they fail to complete repairs within two months of being notified. This should include issues like mould, leaks and critical repairs like toilets, heaters, boilers., Too many landlords fail to complete repairs like mould and leaks in properties, but private tenants have currently no power to end that tenancy early.
 
I want tenants to have the legal right to end their tenancy without any financial backlash, if landlords fail to complete repairs within two months of them being reported. No exit fees and with no possibility of the landlord suing for rent or bills beyond what is owed on the final day of notice given by the tenant.

Fund free care homes for all, irrespective of personal finances, We want the Government to make it so care homes are free to all. We believe it is unfair and unjust that some people pay for care homes and some don’t., If one person doesn't have to pay then neither should anyone else. Many people spend their savings on care, and may then have to sell or release equity on their property to pay for care. People have worked hard for their savings and property and paid their taxes, but then have to spend it on care.

Raise the basic rate of SMP & MA to at least the level of National Minimum Wage, Urgently review and raise maternity pay to at least the national living wage or a % of salary., Today, just over 10% of women benefit from occupational maternity pay. For most maternity leave means a substantial reduction in income to live on less than half of the National Living Wage, or 37% of UK women’s median weekly earnings. 

The financial impact is huge, particularly where women are the highest household earners with nearly 3 in 5 surveyed by Maternity Action forced to return early for financial reasons something that has been shown to impact longer term health and wellbeing.

Abolish leasehold ownership in its entirety, The Leasehold and Freehold Reform Bill does not liberate leaseholders currently living in flats from what we see as a feudal type of ownership., This petition calls for the total abolition of leasehold ownership in the UK, either by amending the current bill or by creating a new one.
 
Leaseholders are left exposed to service charge hikes, ground rents hikes, refusals by some freeholders to extend their leases etc. Many feel they are trapped in flats they cannot sell because of the conditions that come with leasehold ownership.
 
Abolishing leasehold ownership would liberate all leaseholders from this feudal type of ownership. We propose doing so with an eighteen-month notice period, allowing investments in freeholds to be detached in good time.

Abolish the role of Police and Crime Commissioner in England and Wales, We think that Police and Crime Commissioners are ineffective at ensuring that the public's priorities are being reflected by their respective forces, and should be abolished., We think the bedrock on which policing in England is based is public consent. We think this is being eroded, and that PCCs have failed to acknowledge or address this. PCCs have been around for over a decade now, but we believe have not fulfilled their role successfully.

Review the bankruptcy/administration system for corporations, I would like the Government to review the system of bankruptcy and the process of entering liquidation. I believe that, whilst Administrative Protection (under the Insolvency Act 1986) was rightly designed to protect businesses and creditors, the system is now being abused., I believe that the system of acquiring a business and placing it into administration is being abused. Employees made redundant can then have to rely on the taxpayer to cover their redundancy payment through the Redundancy Payments Service. UK landlords can be left with rent unpaid, and UK suppliers left with monies owed. We call for urgent action to protect our taxes.

Make direct debits for vehicle tax payable throughout the month , Vehicle tax can only be paid via direct debit on the first day of each month. The Government should require the DVLA to allow direct debits for vehicle tax to be payable on any day of the month. , Many workers in this country get paid on different dates, putting them at risk of going into tax arrears. I have complained to the DVLA and was told that there is no flexibility as it was set by the Government.
 
In my view, the higher monthly payments should be sufficient to cover the costs incurred by the DVLA in processing the direct debits. I am paid by my employer on 9th of every month. Due to other financial commitments, I need to pay my road tax monthly as it is lower in the short-term. I, and many others, have the added undue stress of ensuring enough money is left to pay my tax.

Disregard partner's income for Universal Credit and tax-free childcare, I would like the Government to base entitlements for Universal Credit and tax-free childcare allowances on the income of the individual claimant, and to disregard the income of any partner., I do not think that the amount of Universal Credit someone receives should take into account their partner's earnings. I also do not think that a partner's income should be considered within eligibility for tax free childcare.

Require businesses give staff the option to be paid monthly, We want the Government to require all businesses to give their staff the option to be paid monthly, to help people manage their finances., Being paid every four weeks, rather than monthly, can make it more difficult to manage personal finances. It can be a particular issue for people claiming Universal Credit, leading to loss of benefits when a claimant is paid twice in a month.

Make it illegal to sell dogs without a licence, We are concerned that not everyone who sells dogs needs a licence, and that some people are stealing dogs, breeding these, and selling dogs without a licence, and dumping no longer wanted dogs. We want anyone who sells a dog, online or offline, to be required to have a licence., We think action is needed to tackle unlicensed sellers of dogs, and believe that the Government should require anyone who sells a dog to be licensed. We think many sellers do not care about the welfare of animals.

Help our sports ground to remain open., Network Rail are in the process of purchasing our sports ground, entrance onto the ground is via a level crossing. The sporting establishment has been in existence for 90 years with zero fatalities or accidents. However, Network Rail want to purchase the ground and close it off to the public., The Perry Barr ward where the ground is located is one of the most deprived wards in the West Midlands. We have over 300 children using this facility with various activities being held during school holidays. With a massive emphasis on green space, mental health and leading active lives for the youngsters of our ward this would be a massive shame for the ground if it was to close. Please help by signing this petition so that we can keep the ground open!!

Change the PTS contracts so they have to be always NHS. Not private contractors, The patient transport needs to stay part of the NHS. Not sold to private contractors. Private contractors do not follow the strict criteria, and often by pass major issues. The vehicles are run down and staff working beyond there abilities due to over worked. Stay pay is horrendous. Look at reviews., The reviews from patients and staff are horrendous about private companies. They see patients as a number and not a human being. Patient care goes straight out the window. With NHS patient transport care is always given and not just a number.
