Fund free train travel for 11-17 year olds, We want the Government to make train travel free for 11 to 17 year olds, as some families are struggling to pay for their child's travel fare to get to school etc due to the cost of living, or losing their jobs., I want the Government to do this is because this should help lots of kids not have to worry about how they will get to school without paying for train fares. I believe the Government will try their best to do everything for the children in the UK. I feel like this should be put in place so parents don’t have to worry about how their children will get to the school.

Continue with the plan for the northern leg of HS2, We feel that cancelling the northern leg of HS2 was a mistake. We think that if HS2 is completed, it will induce huge economical growth in the areas it will connect. We think that cancelling the northern leg of HS2 was a mistake., We think that the UK rail system is already under huge strain. Adding a new high speed line could be a very good investment in the future of the country as a whole, and the more places that are connected the better.

Reform maternity and paternity pay to extend and increase support, We want the Government to reform maternity and paternity pay by extending and increasing support. This could include reforming SMP and SPP payments, reducing the qualifying period for SMP and increasing paternity leave, especially in situations of traumatic births., We want SMP and SPP to be paid at at least minimum wage, with SMP payments paid at full wage for at least 12 weeks and then at the new SMP rate thereafter. We would also like the qualifying period for SMP to be paid to be reduced. This would benefit more mums.
 
We also want Paternity leave to be extended, especially in the cases of traumatic births, with a right to 3 weeks at full pay with the option to take an additional 5 weeks at SPP.

Provide funding to lower the cost of train fares, We want the Government to take action to significant reduce the cost of train fares., Cost of living, rent, petrol, bills and more are going up. This also includes train fares. Why should people be expected to pay £100+ for travel?
 
Train drivers and other staff engage in strike action, but expect a pay increase, yet the public face high prices for often unreliable services.
 
We want the Government to do something now! Help us!

The prices of holidays during school holidays to be reduced, made affordable, I want the prices of holidays to be looked at during school holidays. It is not affordable for most and it’s very unfair that fines are being introduced when it is actually the travel companies that should be held responsible. Why do prices increase so much within a short space of time?, Travel companies should be held responsible. It is not fair that parents are getting fined. I fully appreciate school attendance is important but so is children’s happiness, quality of life, time with loved ones, life experiences, less stress and debt on parents because they want to provide for their children. The cost of living is extremely high, so why not make a change where it hits us the most.

Require train operators to refund tickets if no seats available,  
The Government should require train operators to refund tickets if no seats are available on trains, for at least 75% of their journey. I believe it is not acceptable for passengers to go without seating., Despite electronic ticket barriers gathering data on train usage, I believe there is insufficient seating on the majority of train journeys.
 
Rail fares increase steadily, and I think this is not a question of insufficient data but more related to rail operator profits.

Reform council tax so it is based on square footage and not value, We want council tax bands to be based on square footage of the building, and not the value of the property. We believe current council tax bands aren't fair.
 
, We want the Government to overhaul the council tax system, so this is based on the square footage of the property. We think this would make the tax burden fairer.

Update Universal Credit payments for all claimants from date new rates apply, Universal Credit is paid based on monthly assessment periods. Where an assessment period starts before new rates are introduced, claimants don't benefit from new rates until their next assessment period. We want this to change, so that new rates apply to all claimants as soon as they are introduced., Under the current system claimants can miss out on significant increases in their benefits when Universal Credit allowances are increased in April. I want the Government to change the system so claimants have their Universal Credit payments increased from the day that the changes take affect. At the moment, claimants don’t see the increase until one full assessment period after the rates increase, therefore resulting in many people missing out on between 1 to 30 days at the increased rates.

Extend the Freedom of Information Act to Registered Social Landlords (RSLs)
 
, RSLs exercise functions similar to those of local authorities but are not subject to the same scrutiny. This right could enable tenants and residents to obtain risk assessments, safety certificates, and other documents vital to holding RSLs (and their subsidiaries) to account., This goal can be achieved by amending the Renters (Reform) Bill to designate RSLs (and their subsidiaries) in England and Wales as public authorities for the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act.
 
In Scotland, RSLs are already designated public authorities for the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act.

Create an NHS staff recruitment agency, We urge the government to take action in addressing the NHS's costly reliance on external for-profit staff recruitment agencies. , Supporting the establishment of an NHS-run agency for all staff recruitment & mandating its use for all staff hiring could enable the NHS to save billions of pounds yearly.

In 2019-2020, £6.2 billion was spent on temporary staff, with a significant portion going to agency fees. External agency staff receive higher pay than NHS staff, causing disparity and driving existing staff away, leaving the NHS more dependent on agencies. Savings could be used to increase existing staff wages. We believe that outsourcing recruitment perpetuates a financially unsustainable model that hinders the NHS's ability to deliver cost-effective, high-quality healthcare to the public.
